SPECIFICATION FOR GLASS ALCOHOLOMETERS
PART 1 GLASS ALCOHOLOMETERS WITHOUT THERMOMETER

( First Revision)
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 1 January 1987, after the draft finalized by the Laboratoryware and Related Apparatus Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was originally published as IS : 3608-1966* covering without thermometer. Subsequently, International alcoholometers Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ) brought out the following standards: IS0 IS0 4801-1979 Glass alcoholometers incorporating a thermometer and alcohol hydrometers not

glassware 4805-1982 Laboratory and alcohol-thermo-hydrometers

Thermo-alcoholometer

The Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard decided to revise IS : 3608-1966* to align this standard with the above IS0 Accordingly, this standard has now been revised in two Standards. parts: Part 1 Glass alcoholometers without thermometer; and Part 2 Glass alcoholometers with thermometer. 0.3 In this revision, the alcoholometers having 0.2" graduation ( type Instead two classes B ) have been omitted as the same are not in use. of accuracy have been introduced for glass alcoholometers without thermometer; class A for more accurate work and class B for normal Alcoholometer with thermometer has also been included. work. However, in the case of alcoholometer with thermometer only one type of accuracy, namely class B, has been prescribed. Modifications in dimensions of alcoholometers have been made. Reference temperature has been changed from 15 to 20�C in order to align with the international practice. *Specification for glass alcoholometers. 3

IS : 3608 ( Part 1) - 1987 8. REQUIREMENTS 8.0 Alcoholometers in IS : 9621-1980". 8.1 Materials shall conform with the general requirements given

8.1.1 Glass - The alcoholometers shall be made of colourless transparent glass, resistant to chemicals and thermal shock encountered in use. It shall be as free as possible from strain and visual defects. 8.1.1.1 The be ( 25 + 2 ) x coefficient of cubical thermal lo-6 per degree Celsius. expansion of glass shall

8.1.2 Loading Material - The loading material shall be confined to the bottom of the blub. After the instrument has been maintained in a horizontal position for 1 hour at 80�C and subsequently cooled in that position it shall meet the requirements of 8.2.
NOTE -

The use of mercury as loading material is notpermiited. shall be no loss material Finish whatsoever The in any part of shall

8.1.2.1 There the instrument.

8.2 Pattern, Workmanship and be of a pattern as shown in Fig. 1.

alcoholometer

8.2.1 It shall be circular in cross-section, robust and symmetrical about the main axis. It shall float vertically in alcoholic solutions of appropriate strength and the inclination, if any, from the vertical, shall not exceed 1.5 degrees. 8.3 Scale - The alcoholometer shall have only one scale. The scale and inscriptions shall be marked on a smooth matt surface of white It shall be straight and free from twist. Neither or off-white colour. the scale nor the graduations shall distort or discolour when the alcoholometer is maintained at a temperature of 80�C for 24 hours. The alcoholometer scale shall be fully enclosed in the alcoholometer with all graduation marks clearly visible on the stem. 8.3.1 A reference mark consisting of a short horizontal straight line shall be marked in the paper scale a with a `V' at each end, thus > -< few millimetres above the topmost graduation mark. A fine, clearly etched permanent line of uniform thickness shall be etched on the stem of the alcoholometer coincident with the horizontal portion of the reference mark and slightly longer than that portion of' the reference mark, so that the ends of the etched lines project into the `Vs' at the ends of the reference mark. *Principles of constructions and adjustment of glass hydrometers. 7

8.3.5 Sequence of Graduation Lines - Every tenth graduation line shall be a long line. `There shall be a medium line between two consecutive long lines and four short lind between consecutive medium and long lines. 8.3.6 Figuring of Graduation +&`nes - The highest and the lowest graduation lines referring to the nominal range of the alcoholometer shall be figured in full. NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

APPENDIX ( Clause 8.5.1 )
METHOD A-l. OF TESTING ACCURACY GENERAL

OF ALCOHOLOMETERS

shall be done by one of the Alcoholometer

b) Verifying the readings of alcoholometer at 20�C by determining the density of the liquid at the same temperature by pyknometer and then finding the observed degree corresponding to particular density from Table 1. A-2. COMPARISON METHOD

A-2.1 Readings of the liquid shall be taken simultaneously with the alcoholometer under test and that by a similar but Standard AlcoholoThe readings shall be taken at four or meter under similar conditions. five different points covering the entire range. A-2.2 The readings by alcoholometers shall be taken in a circular or preferably a rectangular vessel suitabIe for the alcoholometer. Dimensions of appropriate vessels are given in Table 3. 11

VERIFICATION

A-3.1 A suitable pyknometer of 25 ml capacity, such as shown in Fig. 2 or pyknometer type 3 of IS : 5717-1970* shall be used. The determination shall be carried out at 20�C. A-3.2 Pour the liquid under test in a weighed pyknometer taking due care that no air is entrapped. Allow the level of the liquid to rise slightly above the mark on the neck of the pyknometer. Place the pyknometer in a bath so that it is immersed in the bath up to a height Maintain the bath at 20�C for about half an slightly below the mark. hour so that the liquid and the pyknometer acquire the temperature of the bath. Adjust the liquid level such that the meniscus just touches Remove the pyknometer the mark on the neck of the pyknometer. from the bath, wipe, dry and weigh; and determine the mass of the liquid. A-3.3 The true mass of the liquid is calculated by adding to the observed mass of the liquid a correction for the buoyancy effect of the air. This correction is calculated from the following formula: c where C = correction density volume observed factor, of experiment, at 2O"C, temperature of and at the in the pyknometer of weights = P( v--m/n)

of air at the temperature in ml of liquid mass in g of the liquid,

m = d =

density of the material experiment.

A-3.4 Calculate the density of the liquid at 20�C by dividing the mass of the liquid as obtained above by volume at 20�C and subsequently from this find out corresponding degree from Table 1. Any departure value in the reading of alcoholometer for the same solution at 20�C separately shall be taken as error at the corresponding point on the scale. *Specification for pyknometers. 12
